Automated Conformance Testing
Pipeline Guide

Continuous spec enforcement for AI-native software delivery

Internal

⚙
Core Principle

The locked openspec.yaml is the contract. The conformance suite is the executable form of that contract. The CI pipeline is the gate that refuses any AI commit that breaks it. Conformance testing is not a phase — it is a continuous, always-on enforcement layer spanning from the first Planning commit through to the Operate phase feedback loop.

RoleConformance Responsibility

Directory Structure
▾

The conformance suite lives alongside specs and is version-controlled as a first-class artifact.

filesystemproject root
specs/
  features/
    <feature-id>/
      openspec.yaml                   ← Locked source of truth (read-only after Gate 1)
      tasks.md                        ← Decomposed tasks with REQ-ID references
      conformance/
        api-tests.yaml                ← Language-agnostic I/O contract (generated by Guardian)

        nfr-targets.yaml              ← Latency, throughput, error-rate budgets (SimLab input)

          <req-id>-input.json
          <req-id>-expected.json

artifacts/
  traceability-report.md             ← REQ-ID → test mapping (generated by TraceGraph)
  test-results.json                  ← Pass/fail record per REQ-ID (generated by Guardian)
  coverage-report.md                 ← Coverage % + unaddressed REQs
  eval-results.json                  ← Semantic scoring per acceptance criterion (EvalHarness)

3
Mapping openspec.yaml to Executable Test Cases
▾

Every requirement in openspec.yaml must produce at least one runnable conformance case before the first line of implementation is written. The six-step extraction process is executed by Guardian in Generation Mode on the first Tuesday of each sprint.

Step-by-Step Extraction

StepActionResponsibleOutput
1Read openspec.yaml; collect all requirements[].id values (REQ-IDs)Guardian—
2For each REQ-ID, parse acceptance_criteria[] — each criterion becomes one test caseGuardian—
3Classify each criterion as functional, data-contract, behavioural, or non-functionalGuardianRouting decision
4Generate test artifact per class: YAML I/O case, .feature scenario, pytest unit, nfr-targets.yaml entryGuardianconformance/ files
5Write REQ-ID → test_file::test_name entries to traceability-report.mdTraceGraphartifacts/traceability-report.md
6Run the full suite against empty stubs — every test MUST fail (Red Baseline)Guardianartifacts/test-results.json
⚑
Red Baseline Rule If any test passes against an empty stub implementation, the test asserts nothing meaningful. Guardian flags these as INVALID in test-results.json and blocks sprint progression until they are corrected.

Acceptance Criterion Classification Rules

ClassPattern in Criterion TextTest Type Generated
Functional"Given / When / Then", input → output assertionsGherkin + pytest-bdd binding
Data-ContractHTTP status codes, response body fields, schema validationYAML I/O case in api-tests.yaml
BehaviouralUser journey steps, UI state transitionsGherkin .feature scenario
Non-FunctionalLatency (p50/p95/p99), error rate, concurrency thresholdsnfr-targets.yaml entry → SimLab
4
What AI Builders Must Check
▾
⚠
Non-Negotiable A Builder who marks a task complete without passing all P0 conformance cases is in violation of Gate 2 conditions.

4.1 Pre-Commit Conformance Checklist

  • Read your task's REQ-ID(s) from tasks.md
  • Run the conformance subset for those REQ-IDs: pytest tests/conformance/ -k "REQ-XXX" -q --tb=short
  • All P0 cases PASS — no exceptions
  • Run spec_diff.py — zero unaddressed REQ-IDs in your assigned scope
  • Provenance headers present in all generated code: @spec: REQ-XXX | @task: TASK-XXX
  • No forbidden-call violations in test output (hallucination guard)
  • Commit message format: feat(REQ-XXX, TASK-XXX): <description>

4.2 Failure Triage Protocol

When a conformance case fails, the Builder must classify the failure before attempting a fix. Misclassification is the primary cause of rework cascades.

CategoryDefinitionCorrect Action
CODE_ERRORThe acceptance criterion is valid; the implementation does not satisfy itFix src/; re-run suite
SPEC_ERRORThe acceptance criterion is ambiguous, contradictory, or technically impossibleDo NOT modify the test or code; raise a SPEC_ERROR comment; POD Lead resolves via spec-amendments.md
ENV_ERRORThe test infrastructure is broken (missing stub, wrong env var, port conflict)Fix the test environment; do NOT modify the test case or implementation
⚑
Critical A Builder who reclassifies a SPEC_ERROR as ENV_ERROR to avoid raising a spec flag is introducing silent drift. InsightOps detects this pattern in test-results.json and escalates to POD Lead.

4.3 Forbidden Patterns — AI Builder Must Never Do These

  • Modify a conformance YAML case to make it pass your implementation
  • Suppress a failing test with pytest.skip() or @pytest.mark.xfail without POD Lead approval
  • Open a PR with a failing P0 case and mark the task "done"
  • Infer what the spec "probably meant" when an acceptance criterion is ambiguous — always SPEC_ERROR
  • Add implementation behaviour not covered by any REQ-ID without creating a new spec amendment
  • Remove a traceability-report.md entry because a requirement was "already covered"

6
Test Runner Implementation
▾

6.1 Python Conformance Runner

pythontests/conformance/test_runner.py
"""
Automation30 Conformance Runner — loads YAML cases and asserts the implementation
against the locked openspec.yaml contract.

Usage:
    pytest tests/conformance/ -q --tb=short
    pytest tests/conformance/ -k "REQ-007" --tb=long
    pytest tests/conformance/ --json-report --json-report-file=artifacts/test-results.json
"""

from pathlib import Path
import yaml, httpx, pytest, re
from unittest.mock import patch

SPEC_DIR = Path("specs/features")
BASE_URL  = "http://localhost:8000"


@pytest.fixture
def db_snapshot(db_session):
    class Snapshot:
        def capture(self):
            from sqlalchemy import text
            snap = Snapshot()
            for table in db_session.execute(
                text("SELECT tablename FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname='public'")
            ).scalars():
                snap._before[table] = db_session.execute(
                    text(f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM {table}")
                ).scalar()
            return snap

        def delta(self, path_expr, before):
            table = path_expr.split(".")[1]
            return self._before.get(table, 0) - before._before.get(table, 0)
    return Snapshot().capture()


def load_cases():
    for yml in SPEC_DIR.rglob("conformance/api-tests.yaml"):
        doc = yaml.safe_load(yml.read_text())
        for case in doc.get("cases", []):
            yield pytest.param(case, id=f"{doc['suite']}::{case['id']}")


@pytest.mark.parametrize("case", load_cases())
def test_conformance(case, db_snapshot, call_recorder):
    method, path = case["endpoint"].split(" ", 1)
    before = db_snapshot

    resp = httpx.request(method, BASE_URL + path,
                         json=case["input"].get("body"),
                         headers=case["input"].get("headers", {}))

    # 1 — Status assertion
    assert resp.status_code == case["expect"]["status"]

    # 2 — Body assertions
    for k, v in case["expect"].get("body_contains", {}).items():
        assert resp.json().get(k) == v

    # 3 — Side-effect assertions
    after = db_snapshot
    for expr, delta in case["expect"].get("side_effects", {}).items():
        assert after.delta(expr, before) == delta

    # 4 — Forbidden-call assertions (hallucination guard)
    for pattern in case.get("forbidden_calls", []):
        regex = re.compile(pattern.replace(".", r"\.").replace("*", ".*"))
        offenders = [c for c in call_recorder.calls if regex.match(c)]
        assert not offenders, f"Forbidden call: {offenders}"

6.2 spec_diff.py — Unaddressed REQ-ID Reporter

pythontools/spec_diff.py
"""
Automation30 spec_diff.py — Reports REQ-IDs with no passing conformance case.
Usage:
    python tools/spec_diff.py artifacts/test-results.json specs/ --fail-on-unaddressed
    python tools/spec_diff.py artifacts/test-results.json specs/ --scope builder-1
"""

import json, sys, argparse
from pathlib import Path
import yaml

def load_req_ids(specs_dir, scope):
    req_ids = set()
    for f in specs_dir.rglob("openspec.yaml"):
        doc = yaml.safe_load(f.read_text())
        for feat in doc.get("features", []):
            for req in feat.get("requirements", []):
                if scope is None or req.get("builder") == scope:
                    req_ids.add(req["id"])
    return req_ids

def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("results_json", type=Path)
    p.add_argument("specs_dir", type=Path)
    p.add_argument("--fail-on-unaddressed", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--scope", default=None)
    args = p.parse_args()

    results = json.loads(args.results_json.read_text())
    passing = {r for t in results.get("tests", [])
               if t.get("outcome") == "passed"
               for r in t.get("req_ids", [])}

    missing = sorted(load_req_ids(args.specs_dir, args.scope) - passing)
    if missing:
        print(f"\n⚠️  UNADDRESSED REQ-IDs ({len(missing)}):")
        for r in missing: print(f"   • {r}")
        if args.fail_on_unaddressed: sys.exit(1)
    else:
        print(f"✅  All REQ-IDs have passing conformance cases.")

if __name__ == "__main__": main()

6.3 AI Builder Self-Verification Hook (Pre-PR Shell Script)

bashautomation30-pre-pr-check.sh
#!/bin/bash
# Run before every PR. Output must be clean before requesting Gate 2 sign-off.
set -e

BUILDER_ID="${1:-}"
RESULTS="artifacts/test-results.json"

# 1. Run conformance suite
pytest tests/conformance/ -q --tb=short --json-report --json-report-file="$RESULTS"

# 2. Report unaddressed REQ-IDs
python tools/spec_diff.py "$RESULTS" specs/ \
  ${BUILDER_ID:+--scope "$BUILDER_ID"} --fail-on-unaddressed

# 3. Check provenance headers
MISSING=$(grep -rL "@spec: REQ-" src/ | grep -E "\.(py|ts|tsx|js)$")
if [ -n "$MISSING" ]; then
  echo "⚠️  Missing @spec provenance headers:" && echo "$MISSING" && exit 1
fi
echo "✅  Pre-PR check complete. Safe to open PR."

Continuous Testing Pipeline — CI/CD Integration
▾

8.1 Pipeline Architecture

Pre-commit
git commit hook
Changed-files conformance subset only. Runs via pre-commit / lefthook.
BLOCK P0
PR Opened
Full conformance suite + SAST + secret scan
GitHub Actions. Triggered on PR creation. Posts conformance summary comment.
BLOCK ANY P0
PR Bot
LLM-as-judge diff review
Custom agent reads openspec.yaml + diff. Posts PASS/FAIL comment per REQ-ID.
COMMENT
Merge Queue
Full suite on rebased HEAD
Re-runs after human approval. Prevents race conditions on parallel PRs.
BLOCK REGR.
Nightly
Full suite on main + spec_diff
Cron 0 2 * * *. Slack alert on regression or unaddressed REQ.
SLACK ALERT
Staging
Integration + full conformance + NFR
Merge to main. Testkube / k6. Blocks production promotion if P0 fails.
BLOCK PROMO
Prod Smoke
P0 subset of api-tests.yaml vs live URL
Post-deploy synthetic monitoring. Triggers rollback procedure if P0 fails.
ROLLBACK

8.2 GitHub Actions — PR Conformance Gate

yaml.github/workflows/conformance.yml
name: automation30-conformance-gate
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, "sprint/**"]

concurrency:
  group: conformance-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  conformance:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16
        env: { POSTGRES_PASSWORD: test, POSTGRES_DB: automation30_test }
        options: --health-cmd pg_isready --health-interval 5s --health-retries 5
        ports: ["5432:5432"]

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: { python-version: "3.12", cache: pip }
      - run: pip install -r requirements.txt
      - run: alembic upgrade head
        env: { DATABASE_URL: postgresql://postgres:test@localhost/automation30_test }
      - name: Start application
        run: |
          uvicorn src.app:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 &
          sleep 5 && curl --fail http://localhost:8000/health
      - name: Run conformance suite
        run: |
          pytest tests/conformance/ -q --tb=short \
            --json-report --json-report-file=artifacts/test-results.json
      - name: Spec coverage check
        run: |
          python tools/spec_diff.py artifacts/test-results.json specs/ \
            --fail-on-unaddressed
      - name: Static analysis + secret scan
        run: ruff check src/ && bandit -r src/ -ll
      - name: Comment conformance summary on PR
        if: always()
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const report = require('./artifacts/test-results.json');
            const { passed, failed, total } = report.summary;
            const status = failed > 0 ? '❌ BLOCKED' : '✅ PASS';
            await github.rest.issues.createComment({
              ...context.repo, issue_number: context.issue.number,
              body: `## Spec Conformance — ${status}\nPassed: ${passed} / ${total}`
            });

8.4 Branch Protection Rules (Non-Negotiable)

⚑
Hard Rules Required status checks: conformance, lint, sast. Required reviews: ≥1 human POD Lead. Dismiss stale approvals on new commits. Block force-push to main and specs/**. Conformance cases are immutable post-Red-Baseline — protected under tests/conformance/**.
9
How the Suite Grows with Every New Spec
▾

The conformance suite is self-expanding. Every time SpecFlow produces a new or updated openspec.yaml, new conformance cases are generated automatically and appended to the suite without manual intervention.

9.1 New Spec → New Cases Flow

1. SpecFlow writes openspec.yaml for a new feature
           │
           ▼
2. POD Lead locks the spec (Gate 1 sign-off)
   openspec.yaml: status: draft → locked
           │
           ▼
3. Guardian detects new REQ-IDs not in traceability-report.md
   (set(openspec REQ-IDs) - set(traceability-report REQ-IDs))
           │
           ▼
4. Guardian appends new cases to api-tests.yaml, acceptance.feature, nfr-targets.yaml
           │
           ▼
5. TraceGraph updates traceability-report.md — new entries at Status: PENDING
           │
           ▼
6. Guardian runs Red Baseline on new cases only — all must FAIL
           │
           ▼
7. conformance-delta.md written — lists new REQ-IDs and confirms RED baseline

9.2 Mid-Sprint Spec Change Handling

⚠
Post-Gate 1 Changes Require POD Lead Approval SpecImpactAnalyzer runs first to produce impact-analysis.md and rework-scope-patch.yaml. Gate 2 re-fires against fresh artifacts for all Builder tasks that depend on changed REQ-IDs (rework ripple).

9.3 Spec Version Pinning

Every conformance case carries a spec_version field. The runner validates this on execution to prevent stale cases from passing silently against a newer spec.

pythontests/conformance/test_runner.py — version guard
def test_spec_version_integrity(case):
    feature_id = case["id"].split("_")[0]
    spec_path = Path(f"specs/features/{feature_id}/openspec.yaml")
    current_version = yaml.safe_load(spec_path.read_text()).get("version")

    assert case.get("spec_version") == current_version, (
        f"Case '{case['id']}' was generated against spec v'{case.get('spec_version')}' "
        f"but current openspec is v'{current_version}'. Re-run Guardian (Generation Mode)."
    )
ℹ
Audit Trail Preservation Rule A conformance case is never deleted when a spec changes. It is superseded — the old case moves to conformance/history/ and a new case is written with a new ID.

11
Hallucination Guard — Forbidden-Call Enforcement
▾

Every conformance case that includes a forbidden_calls list is testing for AI Builder hallucination — specifically, unrequested calls to external services or behaviours not specified in the openspec.

How It Works

  1. The call_recorder fixture intercepts all outbound HTTP calls during test execution.
  2. After each test, the runner compares recorded calls against forbidden_calls regex patterns in the YAML case.
  3. A match triggers a test failure classified as HALLUCINATION_GUARD_VIOLATION in test-results.json.
  4. InsightOps surfaces patterns of the same forbidden call appearing across multiple cases as a SYSTEMIC_HALLUCINATION finding in spec-amendments.md.

Common Forbidden-Call Patterns

yamlconformance/api-tests.yaml — forbidden_calls
forbidden_calls:
  - "external.email-verify.*"     # REQ called for internal format check only
  - "external.fraud-score.*"      # Not in scope for this sprint
  - "external.geocoding.*"        # Address storage only; no geo enrichment
  - "storage.audit-log.*"         # Do not log rejected payloads with PII
  - "ai.llm.*"                    # This path must be deterministic — no LLM call

8
Invoke EvalHarness: "Score [builder-id]'s output for REQ-[XXX] against the spec" — establish eval rubric
9
Builders begin implementation; run automation30-pre-pr-check.sh before first commit
Days 3–4 — Tuesday–Thursday (Continuous Build)
10
Each Builder commit triggers the PR conformance gate automatically
11
Guardian (Execution Mode) runs on each commit; test-results.json updated
12
RedTeamX, SimLab, PolicyEnforcer run mid-sprint
13
Failing cases triaged per Section 4.2 — CODE_ERROR / SPEC_ERROR / ENV_ERROR
Day 5 — Thursday EOD
14
InsightOps synthesises all outputs → validation-report.md
15
POD Lead reviews Gate 2 conditions (Section 10)
16
Any SPEC_ERROR findings routed back to SpecFlow for next sprint
Day 6 — Friday (Release)
17
ReleaseIntel reads coverage-report.md for Gate 3
18
Gate 3 conditions met → POD Lead signs release attestation
19
Nightly job active; pipeline is now live for all future sprints
